Rajeev Juneja: 
Thank you, Archit. A very good evening to all of you. Welcome to Q2 & H1 FY27 earning call. 
At Mankind, our strategy is centered around three priorities; strengthening our core business, 
scaling chronic and specialty therapies and investing in future growth platforms. We made 
steady progress across each of these during the quarter, resulting in another period of strong 
operating performance. During the quarter, overall revenue increased to Rs. 4,338 crores, up 
17% year-on-year, while EBITDA for the quarter increased by 27.2% to Rs. 1,175 crores and 
EBITDA margin improved by 210 bps year-on-year to 27.1%.

BSVs portfolio continued its 20%+ growth momentum for the second consecutive quarter, led 
by strong performance in both domestic and international markets.  
Revenues of domestic business excluding consumer healthcare increased by 15.9% year-on-year 
to Rs. 3,428 crores in Q2 & H1 FY27, driven by strong double-digit growth in both Mankind 
and BSV specialty business.  
Mankind's strong foundations, combined with disciplined execution over last few quarters, have 
resulted in outperformance to IPM in Q2 FY27. According to IQVIA, our secondary sales grew 
by 15.7%, representing a 1.1x outperformance versus the IPM growth of 14.2% excluding 
tirzepatide. This was largely driven by a 1.2x volume outperformance, continued strength in 
chronic therapies and strong recovery in key acute therapies led by gastro and vitamins. 
Our initiatives across leadership and field changes, process optimization, focus product 
portfolio, doctor's engagement and extensive use of technology have resulted in improving 
volume growth trend from 0.5% growth in FY25 to 2.3% volume growth in FY26, 4.7% volume 
growth in 1st Quarter this year to now outperforming IPM with a volume growth of 6.2% in 
Quarter 2. 
One of our key strategic priorities has been to increase the contribution of chronic therapies 
through focused initiatives including medico marketing, new product launches, in-licensing and 
selective brand acquisitions. We have consistently outperformed the chronic market and 
strengthened our position in key therapies areas. As a result, our chronic share excluding BSV 
expanded by 80 bps year-on-year to 37.4% led by 1.1x outperformance in cardio and anti-
diabetes excluding tirzepatide and a strong 1.9x outperformance in chronic respiratory during 
the quarter.  
While we are expanding our recently launched multi-therapy mass-market division - Vistaar, we 
are also progressing towards the launch of new divisions in cardio, gastro and dental therapies. 
These divisions will enhance focus on high potential brands and improve specialist engagement 
to accelerate growth. 
Our consumer healthcare business delivered a revenue of Rs. 229 crores in Q2FY27, impacted 
by slower offtake in category for the industry and some regional impact in East and South. 
Despite softer growth, we gained market share in key brands like Manforce and Preganews. Our 
modern trade and e-commerce share increased to 18% from 12% a year ago supported by 55% 
growth in that channel. 
Innovation and specialization continue to remain central to our long-term strategy and we are 
steadily building differentiated science-led pipeline that complements our existing portfolio. 
Happy to share our in-house pipeline asset MKP11093, a best-in-class JAK Inhibitor has 
received funding under PRIP program by the Government of India, a first for Mankind.

As our business continues to evolve, we are seeing the benefits of strategic choices made over 
the past few years. The quarter was marked by strong operating momentum and continued 
advancement of our long-term priorities. 
Let me take you through the key developments: 
Our domestic business delivered another quarter of strong growth with revenue increasing by 
14.8% year-on-year to Rs 3,657 crores. This was driven by 16% growth in Mankind core 
domestic, ex-consumer and mid-teen growth in BSV domestic business, partially impacted by 
muted growth in consumer healthcare.  
Importantly, we continued to outperform the IPM led by 1.1x outperformance in chronic, with 
19% year-on-growth in cardiac and 16% growth in anti-diabetic. Recovery in acute continued 
with 1.1x outperformance driven by 26% year-on-year growth in vitamin and mineral and 19% 
growth in gastro, further supported by key brands such as Gudcef, Pantakind and Dydroboon. 
Anti-infective continues to recover quarter-on-quarter with a growth of 5.4% in Q2FY27 versus 
3.6% in Q1FY27. BSV business also delivered strong momentum with robust growth in key 
brands – Humog (51%), Lonopin (45%), Anti-D (37%) and ASVS (45%).  
Another encouraging aspect is the increasing scale of our brand portfolio. We have added 9 new 
brand families with sales over Rs. 50 crores taking the total to 63 in MAT September 26 versus 
54 in Financial Year ’26, and 4 brand families with sales over Rs. 100 crores taking the total to 
26 from 22 during the same period. This reflects the continued productivity and scalability of 
our commercial engine. Additionally, we are seeing encouraging traction across our newer 
brands including Vonalong, Empagreat, Dynaduo, Nurokind HS PFS and Pantakind Raft.

performance for Q2 FY27: 
Our revenue from operations during Q2 FY27 has increased by 17.3% year-on-year basis to Rs 
4,338 crores as compared to Rs 3,697 crores in Q2 FY26 driven by strong growth in our base 
business as well as BSV specialty business.  
Our gross margins for the quarter has increased by 90 basis point year-on-year basis to 72.2% 
from 71.3% in Q2 FY26. This year-on-year increase is primarily driven by three factors. Firstly, 
the impact of sales price increase which we have taken. Secondly, the favourable sales mix as 
our chronic contribution has increased by 80 basis point on a year-on-year basis. And lastly, 
there has been a favourable base effect as Q2 last year, our gross margins were compressed due 
to GST 2.0 transitioning impact.

Our reported EBITDA margin for the quarter has increased to 27.1% as compared to 25.0% in 
Q2 FY26. This increase of 210 basis point is primarily driven by three factors. 90 basis point 
increase is from gross margin expansion, reduced R&D expense by 40 basis point and the 
balance 80 basis point benefit has come from operating leverage due to sales growth.  
The EBITDA margins for H1 FY27 is 26.7% which has increased by 230 basis point year-on-
year basis. The improvement is primarily due to increase in gross margins by 160 basis point 
and the balance 70% benefit has come from operating leverage.  
The R&D expenses for the quarter was Rs. 108 crores which is at 2.5% of sales and the same is 
lower than R&D spend of 2.9% of sales during Q2 FY26. This 2.5% is lower than our guidance 
of 3% for the full year FY27. 
The finance cost for Q2 FY27 has declined to Rs. 105 crores from Rs. 110 crores during Q1 
FY27 as Q1 FY27 had a NCD repayment of Rs. 1,250 crores. 
In Q2 FY27 the depreciation and amortization expenses has increased to Rs. 236 crores as 
compared to Rs. 222 crores in Q2 FY26. This is in line with the asset capitalization undertaken 
during the period.  
The effective tax rate for H1 FY27 was at 24% which has increased from 17.1% in H1 FY26. 
The increase in effective tax rate is due to adoption of new tax regime this year following the 
expiry of the tax exemption period.  
The profit after tax for Q2 FY27 grew by 37.7% year-on-year basis to Rs. 716 crores with PAT 
margins improving to 16.5% during the quarter as compared to 14.1% in Q2 FY26 resulting in 
an increase of 240 basis point. This growth was primarily driven by stronger EBITDA margins 
and lower finance cost which has got partially offset because of increased ETR. 
Our diluted EPS is Rs. 17.2 per share of Rs. 1 paid for the quarter. The cash EPS which is EPS 
adjusted for non-cash items like depreciation and amortization has increased during the quarter 
to Rs. 22.9 from Rs. 17.7 in Q2 FY26 an increase of 29.1% year-on-year basis.  
The net operating working capital for the quarter on trailing 12-month basis has increased to 51 
days as compared to 46 days in the corresponding period last year mainly due to increased 
working capital. 
In H1 FY27 our cash flow from operations has increased to Rs. 1,819 crores as compared to Rs. 
1,637 crores in H1 FY26 which is on a year-on-year basis an increase of 11.1%. In H1 FY27 our 
cash flow to EBITDA ratio has decreased to 81% as compared to 92% in H1 FY26. The drop of 
11% in cash flow to EBITDA is due to increased working capital.
